meta.title: Upstream fixes visible: policy-anchor validation and trace forwarding, plus regression set
meta.battery: Upstream-inspired cycle: filesystem-policy anchors (#5278), trace-context env forwarding (#2931), plus reruns of env injection, label selector, concurrent exec.

results.title: Filesystem policy anchors (upstream #5278)
results.desc: Valid absolute RO/RW anchors accepted+stored; relative anchor rejected
results.detail: valid anchors (/srv/data RO, /tmp/rwdir RW) created+Ready+stored; relative anchor rejected grpc=3: policy contains unsafe content: sandbox policy validation failed; path must be absolute (start with '/'): relative
results.prose: I encode a filesystem policy with an absolute read-only anchor (/srv/data) and read-write anchor (/tmp/rwdir), then one with a relative path. The valid one came up Ready with both anchors stored; the relative one was rejected with INVALID_ARGUMENT: "policy contains unsafe content: sandbox policy validation failed; path must be absolute". This is upstream fix #5278 (merged 2026-11-06) visibly enforced on this gateway — sandbox policy anchors are validated, not just stored.
steps: grep upstream commits; identify fix(sandbox): validate filesystem policy anchors (#5278)
Poll GetSandbox until Ready; verify anchors stored in spec
CreateSandbox with relative path anchor; expect INVALID_ARGUMENT (grpc=3)

results.title: Trace-context env forwarding (upstream #2931)
results.desc: W3C traceparent delivered to sandbox env
results.prose: Upstream #2931 forwards W3C trace context (TRACEPARENT/TRACESTATE) from CLI to gateway for CI trace continuity. I set a synthetic traceparent in the sandbox env spec and echoed it back from inside the sandbox: it arrived byte-for-byte. The user-visible half of trace continuity — context reaching the workload — holds on this gateway; server-side OTel correlation isn't observable from here.
steps: grep upstream commits; identify feat(cli): forward TRACEPARENT/TRACESTATE (#2931)
CreateSandbox with env TRACEPARENT=00-ce6aeb4f...-42e0b743...-01 (synthetic W3C trace context)

results.title: Random env injection
results.desc: Two random env vars verified in exec
results.prose: Two randomly generated env vars injected at sandbox creation both came back verbatim from an exec inside it. Env propagation is the baseline every credential-injection and trace-forwarding feature depends on, so I keep it in the mix every cycle.
steps: Generate 2 random key=value env pairs from seed

results.title: Random label selector
results.prose: A sandbox created with this cycle's random label pair was matched by a label selector listing — only the labeled sandbox returned. Label selectors are how workloads find their sandboxes; a regression here would break orchestration quietly.
steps: Verify exactly one match: this sandbox

results.title: Random-width concurrent exec
results.prose: Five concurrent exec streams against one sandbox, each returning a computed value seeded per cycle. All five outputs were correct, so the gateway serialized the streams without crosstalk — the concurrency path stays healthy under fan-out.
steps: Parallel ExecSandbox calls with per-thread temp files, each echoing computed w<i>-<n>
Verify every stream returns its own value
